guide.label: Client-side rendering
guide.description: The browser receives a basic page and JavaScript, then builds the interface and may fetch data after loading.

guide.label: Server-side rendering
guide.description: HTML is generated when a request arrives, so the initial response can show current content.

guide.label: Static site generation
guide.description: HTML is prepared at build time and served as already generated files; changes appear after a rebuild.

guide.label: Hydration
guide.description: Client-side event handlers are attached to HTML already rendered by the server or build process.

comparison.label: Stable help page
comparison.description: Static generation fits content that rarely changes.

comparison.label: Public page needing current data
comparison.description: Server-side rendering fits when information must be current when requested.

comparison.label: Interactive signed-in dashboard
comparison.description: Client-side rendering can be a reasonable choice for frequent interaction.

questions.prompt: When does static site generation prepare HTML?
choices: After JavaScript loads in the browser
questions.explanation: Static site generation prepares HTML ahead of time, during the build.
questions.quote: Static site generation prepares HTML at build time.

questions.prompt: When does server-side rendering generate HTML?
questions.explanation: Server-side rendering generates HTML for each incoming request.
questions.quote: Server-side rendering generates HTML when a request arrives.

questions.prompt: Which approach suits a frequently used interactive dashboard behind sign-in?
questions.explanation: The notes say client-side rendering can be a reasonable choice for an interactive signed-in dashboard.
questions.quote: For a frequently used interactive dashboard behind sign-in, client-side rendering can be a reasonable choice.

questions.prompt: Why can a page show content before some controls are interactive?
choices: The server is still rendering the HTML
JavaScript has not yet attached event handlers through hydration
questions.explanation: Hydration attaches event handlers after the HTML is displayed, so controls can briefly be inactive.
questions.quote: A page may display its content before JavaScript makes some controls interactive.

questions.prompt: With static site generation, when do content changes appear?
choices: After a rebuild or another supported refresh mechanism
When the browser fetches data after loading
questions.explanation: Pre-built files only change after a rebuild or another supported refresh.
questions.quote: Content changes appear after a rebuild or another supported refresh mechanism.
